svg.aria-label: Diagram contrasting two kinds of account baseline control. On the left, reversible controls — account-level S3 Block Public Access, EBS encryption by default, Region restriction, root user hardening — which have the same effect whenever they are switched on, so the cost of lateness is the exposure window plus remediating whatever was created meanwhile. On the right, path-dependent controls — an organisation CloudTrail trail, the Config recorder, GuardDuty — which produce a record, and the record for the period before they were enabled does not exist and cannot be created. Below, a timeline showing that CloudTrail Event history covers only the past 90 days, so an account with no trail loses its evidence on a rolling basis.
svg.title: Reversible versus path-dependent account baseline controls, and the ninety-day evidence cliff
svg.text: Two kinds of baseline control, and only one can be added later
The difference is not importance. It is whether the control's value depends on having been there from the beginning.
Reversible — the same effect whenever you switch it on
• S3 Block Public Access, at the account level
• EBS encryption by default
• Region restriction
• Root user MFA, no access keys, alternate contacts
The cost of lateness is the exposure window, plus
remediating whatever was created meanwhile. Both are
real, and both are bounded and payable.
Expensive to add late. Possible to add late.
Path-dependent — the value is in having been there
• An organisation CloudTrail trail
• The AWS Config recorder
• GuardDuty
• IAM Access Analyzer, and anything else that emits findings
These produce a record. The record for the period before
you enabled them does not exist, and no amount of
money or effort creates it afterwards.
Not expensive to add late. Impossible to add late.
The grace period, and why it is the dangerous shape
account created
day 90
you go looking
Event history covers this
Nothing here survives without a trail. It is already gone by the time you need it.
Why an unaudited account looks healthy right up to the moment it does not
CloudTrail is on by default and free, so the console always shows recent activity. It is a rolling 90-day window, one account, one Region,
with no organisation aggregation — which is indistinguishable from working until somebody asks about the fourth month.
This is the whole argument for a baseline over a checklist: a checklist item done late is late, and three of these items done late are simply not done.
